Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-33562eae (solved)

## Verified rule: extend every adjacent same-color pair as a ray
For each pair of same-colored cells that form a local vector (the markers in these examples are adjacent diagonally or horizontally), continue that vector beyond the second marker one cell at a time, to the grid boundary. Keep all input cells unchanged and preserve the background. Distinct marker pairs/colors can yield multiple rays; trace each on the same grid. The verified examples show rays can overlap/interact, but original marks remain.

A reliable way to infer direction is to view the two markers in their displayed order: from first to second, calculate `(dr, dc)` and continue from the second by that same displacement. Check the orientation in the output examples: rays extend along their marker pair's direction, not in both directions.

## Demo 1 evidence (14x16, background 7)
- Color 6 at (r7,c8),(r8,c9): vector down-right; output extends through (r13,c14), stopping at boundary.
- Color 4 at (r7,c11),(r8,c10): vector down-left; output adds (r9,c9),(r10,c8),(r11,c7),(r12,c6),(r13,c5).
- Color 8 at (r9,c9),(r10,c8): vector down-left; output continues to (r13,c5).
- Color 9 at (r9,c10),(r10,c11): vector down-right; output continues through (r13,c14).
These demonstrate that the pair itself stays as given and the ray fills subsequent diagonal positions to the edge.

## Solved test (13x23, background 2)
Input marker pairs:
- 8: (r2,c14),(r3,c15), vector (+1,+1); extend down-right from (r3,c15), through (r12,c24) but columns end at 22, so actual ray positions within grid: (r4,c16) onward to (r9,c21); (r10,c22) is in bounds, and (r11,c23) is out of bounds. Note: the supplied correct output retained only original 8s and did not draw a ray for this color; see qualification below.
- 7: (r2,c17),(r3,c16), vector (+1,-1); correct output extended from the second mark down-left at (r4,c15), (r5,c14), ... (r12,c7).
- 5: (r4,c15),(r5,c14), vector (+1,-1); correct output extended down-left at (r6,c13), (r7,c12), ... (r12,c7).
- 3: (r4,c16),(r5,c17), vector (+1,+1); correct output extended down-right at (r6,c18), (r7,c19), (r8,c20), (r9,c21), (r10,c22), ending at right edge.

The exact selection rule for why 8 is not extended is not established; do not confidently extend every pair in future tasks without considering layout-specific selection. All color-5 and color-7 rays overlap at diagonal cells (r7,c12 onward) in the submitted grid, with the output showing 5 on this shared diagonal; importantly the correct output confirmed the specific resulting grid.

No added 8 cells. This case confirms extension is based on the same-color adjacent pair's oriented vector and rays terminate at the grid boundary, but it also shows the candidate 8 pair may be a non-extending/overlapping guide; investigate rather than assume all pairs extend if a future example presents similar multi-pair geometry.
